body.prose:
Holons have to have ids I think and have to have commits.

I don't think we can base ourselves on git here. So if we do ourselves, implementation is not as necessary as the data over the wire, the protocol existing or new and if existing which and in what format.

I know nothing about the mentioned things here, we need grounding and I need some background here, history and culture as well, and to understand what kind of box you are drawing and what is outside the box.

So the question remains, should we select this. Is there something else that makes more sense? Should we make our own. How aligned is it with the vision of OpenLight? Will we have to let this go down the line? Because it doesn't work for us. How much do we gain by adopting it now? Should we leave it untouched for now, since we're just storing staticness anyway? Is what we're looking at just a standard? Or does it actually come with a faster delivery?

Sounds reasonable. Nothing in the previous [OpenLight] studies goes against it. Sounds good, but what does that mean? Where is the data stored? How is it served?
body.title: Ids, commits, and the wire
